title: Bond-clean verification, defects and photographic handover
audience: Bond and end-of-lease cleaners who verify the clean and hand it over to the customer.
referencesAtStart: Official sources: Consumer Affairs Victoria, Condition reports (renting) (last updated 14 October 2026); Consumer Affairs Victoria, Releasing or claiming the bond (landlords and owners) (last updated 14 October 2026); Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC), Small business and the Privacy Act (published 10 March 2023; last modified 5 September 2024); Consumer Affairs Victoria, Moving out of a rental property (last updated 14 October 2026); Residential Tenancies Authority Queensland, Carpet cleaning and pest control (no date shown).
learningOutcomes: Inspect against the signed checklist, not subjective impressions.
Classify findings as missed cleaning, pre-existing wear, permanent damage, inaccessible or out of scope.
Hand over with approved evidence, exceptions and follow-up, without guaranteeing a bond outcome.

instruction.heading: Inspect against the agreed list
instruction.body:
Inspect with the signed checklist in your hand, not with a general impression of the room. The checklist was agreed and signed before the work started, and it names each surface, fixture and standard that the clean covers. Walk the property in the same order as the checklist, so that nothing is skipped and the record can be checked line by line later. Use a good light, held low across walls and cupboard fronts where marks show best, and check from the doorway and from close up.

Check the accessible surfaces, the corners, the top of the door frames, the inside of cupboards that were agreed to be cleaned, the rear of the toilet and the basin, the gaps around the cooktop, and the floor edges and skirting. A room that looks clean from the doorway can still have missed cleaning in those places. Confirm that products have been rinsed or removed as the label requires, because residue can look like a stain or a film. If a line on the checklist cannot be checked, mark it as inaccessible rather than passing it.

instruction.heading: Classify findings fairly
instruction.body:
Separate each finding into one of five groups. Missed cleaning is an area that the agreed clean covered and did not clean properly, and it is corrected. Pre-existing wear is a mark or condition that was present before the clean, and the pre-work record shows it. Permanent damage is a defect that cleaning will not remove, such as a crack, a chip or a burn, and it is recorded and referred for assessment. Inaccessible means the area could not be reached safely or without damage, and the reason is recorded. Out of scope means the item was not part of the agreed clean, and it is recorded as such.

Do not alter the evidence to fit a classification. Do not imply that a stain is removable until it has been assessed, and do not describe a permanent defect as cleaning. An inspector who flags a cracked tile may be looking at damage that was present before the clean, and the pre-work record shows it. Compare the finding with the photographs and notes from the start of the job. Where the record does not show the condition, say so, and do not claim that it was present or absent.

instruction.heading: Standards, reports and what the checklist is
instruction.body: The standard a renter must meet is set by the tenancy law of the state or territory, and it varies. In Victoria, the Consumer Affairs Victoria guidance says that a renter must leave the property reasonably clean and in the same condition as when they moved in, allowing for fair wear and tear. For rental agreements signed from 29 March 2021, the page says a rental provider cannot require professional cleaning unless the property needs to be returned to its starting state, or is in a state that requires professional cleaning. It does not require renters to use a particular cleaner (Consumer Affairs Victoria, moving out of a rental property; last updated 14 October 2026). In Queensland, the Residential Tenancies Authority page says a tenant must leave the property in the same condition as at the start, apart from fair wear and tear, and that a landlord or property manager cannot require a better condition, require a particular cleaning or pest service or provider, or require a set fee for it (RTA Queensland, carpet cleaning and pest control page; no date shown). In Victoria, the rental provider or agent completes the exit condition report, within 10 days after the rental agreement ends. The renter must be present or have a reasonable opportunity to attend. The exit section is part of the original condition report, and bond-claim evidence such as invoices, receipts, quotes or photographs must be given to the renter at least 3 business days before a claim is made (Consumer Affairs Victoria, condition reports; last updated 14 October 2026). Your checklist is a separate record of the clean. It is not the condition report, and it must not be presented as one.

instruction.heading: Evidence, bond release and the handover
instruction.body:
Take authorised photographs that show the area and its context, with the timestamp on. Avoid people, private documents, mail and personal possessions in the frame. Obtain the occupant's and the owner's consent before photographing their property, and keep the originals and their timestamps under the business's retention and access rules. Store them securely and share them only with the people entitled to them.

Bond release in Victoria is decided by the parties named on the bond, or by an order. The Consumer Affairs Victoria page says the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority repays a bond when everyone listed agrees, or when the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal, or Rental Dispute Resolution Victoria for a binding order, has made an order. A renter who starts a claim gives the other parties 14 days to contest it, and the bond may be repaid as the claim directs if nobody contests it (Consumer Affairs Victoria, releasing or claiming the bond; last updated 14 October 2026). Your handover does not decide that outcome, so do not guarantee acceptance by a property manager, the return of a security deposit, or the release of a bond.

Correct any missed cleaning, reinspect the corrected area against the checklist, and record that you did so. Record what could not be resolved within scope. Then give the customer the completed checklist, the exceptions and classifications, the approved photographs and the follow-up contact. Describe the clean and the evidence only. The local law and the manufacturer's instructions govern, and this lesson does not substitute for them.

procedure: Inspect accessible surfaces in checklist order, under a suitable light, from the doorway and close up.
Confirm that products have been rinsed or removed as the label requires, and check hidden areas listed on the checklist.
Correct missed cleaning and reinspect the corrected area against the checklist.
Classify each remaining finding as missed cleaning, pre-existing, permanent, inaccessible or out of scope, and check it against the pre-work record.
Take authorised photographs with timestamps that avoid people, private documents and personal possessions.
Hand over the completed checklist, the classifications, the approved evidence and the follow-up contact, without a bond or deposit guarantee.

workedExamples.situation: An inspector flags a cracked tile as poor cleaning, and a dusty shelf is overlooked during the clean.
workedExamples.reasoning: Supply the pre-work evidence that shows the cracked tile was pre-existing damage, and record it as permanent damage that cleaning will not remove. Separately correct the overlooked dusty shelf as missed cleaning, reinspect it against the checklist and record the result. Report both outcomes in the handover, with the photographs and the classifications, and do not argue the bond outcome.

workedExamples.situation: An agent asks the cleaner to confirm in writing that the bond will be returned in full once the clean is finished.
workedExamples.reasoning: Decline to give that confirmation. The bond outcome is decided by the parties named on the bond, or by an order, as the state's rules set out. Confirm what the clean covered, the checklist that was completed, the classifications, the corrections made and the evidence provided. Offer the handover pack and the follow-up contact instead.

workedExamples.situation: A photograph taken during the clean shows a family member in the background and a letter on the kitchen bench.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the photograph?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not supply the photograph as it is. Remove it from the handover set, retake it so that the person and the letter are not in the frame, and store the original under the business's retention and access rules. Record the retake in the job notes, and check the other photographs for the same issue before handover.

equipmentAndPpe: Signed checklist, with the agreed scope and acceptance criteria.
Inspection light for checking surfaces at a low angle.
Camera or phone for authorised photographs, with timestamps on.
Reinspection sheet and the pre-work record for comparison.
Handover pack with the checklist, classifications, approved photographs and follow-up contact.

commonErrors.prevention: Use the signed checklist line by line, and mark any line that cannot be checked as inaccessible.

commonErrors.error: Calling pre-existing damage a cleaning failure, or the reverse.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the pre-work record, classify the finding, and state what the record does and does not show.

commonErrors.error: Promising bond return or acceptance at handover.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the clean and the evidence only, and refer bond questions to the parties or the tribunal.

commonErrors.error: Presenting the cleaning checklist as the condition report.
commonErrors.prevention: Label the checklist as the cleaning record. The exit condition report is completed by the rental provider or agent under the state's rules.

commonErrors.error: Photographing people, private documents or possessions.
commonErrors.prevention: Frame each photograph on the surface and fixture only, and retake any photograph that shows personal items.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Whether the federal Privacy Act applies to photographs taken during a bond clean depends on the business. Most businesses with annual turnover of $3 million or less are outside the Act, but some small businesses are covered regardless of turnover, including health service providers and businesses that trade in personal information (OAIC, small business page; last modified 5 September 2024). Obtain the occupant's and the owner's consent before photographing their property.

Victoria: the rental provider or agent completes the exit condition report within 10 days after the agreement ends, and the cleaner's checklist is a separate record (Consumer Affairs Victoria; last updated 14 October 2026). Queensland: the RTA page states the same-condition and no-provider-requirement points noted in this lesson, and the page mentions a March 2018 prosecution and a 2019 QCAT appeal, without a last-updated date (RTA Queensland; no date shown).
Conditions vary by state, territory and country. The local law and the manufacturer's instructions govern, and this lesson does not substitute for them.

qualityStandard: The checklist is completed line by line in the simulated inspection, with any inaccessible line marked.
Each finding is classified against the pre-work record, and missed cleaning is corrected and reinspected.
The handover contains the checklist, the classifications, the approved photographs and the follow-up contact, with no bond or deposit guarantee.
No photograph in the handover shows people, private documents or personal possessions.
documentationEvidence: Completed signed checklist with a classification for each finding.
Authorised photographs with timestamps, and a record of any retake.
Reinspection record for each corrected area.
Handover record with the follow-up contact, and the client's acknowledgement of receipt.
summary: Inspect against the signed list, line by line, and mark what cannot be checked.
Classify findings fairly against the pre-work record, and keep the evidence unaltered.
Hand over the record and the evidence without guaranteeing a bond or deposit outcome.

knowledgeChecks.question: How should the final inspection be done?
options: By general impression of the room as a whole
Against the signed checklist, line by line
By the customer's opinion alone, not the list
By looking only from the doorway at the room

knowledgeChecks.question: A cracked tile is flagged. Pre-work evidence shows it was there before the clean. How is it recorded?
options: As missed cleaning, since the tile was not wiped during the clean
As the cleaner's fault, recorded against the cleaning contractor
As pre-existing damage, and classified against the pre-work record
As a bond deduction the cleaner must pay, since the tile was damaged

knowledgeChecks.question: What must the handover avoid?
options: Listing the exceptions found during the final walk through the rooms
Attaching the signed checklist, which records each line of the clean
Guaranteeing acceptance by the agent or the return of the bond
Describing the corrections made after the first inspection
